title: Declared fields, public fields, every field

blocks.text: `getFields()` and `getDeclaredFields()` differ in two ways, visibility and inheritance:
Neither gives every field, private inherited ones included: for that you walk up with `getSuperclass()`.

items: `ownFields(type)`: the fields `type` itself declares, **every access level**, sorted.
`publicFields(type)`: every public field, **inherited ones too**, including the **constants of interfaces** `type` implements, sorted.
`allFields(type)`: every field of `type` and of **each superclass up to the top**, any access level. `type`'s own names first (sorted), then its parent's (sorted), and so on.

blocks.text: With `Parent { public publicField; private privateField; }` and `Child extends Parent implements Tagged { public childPublic; private childPrivate; }`, where `Tagged` declares `String TAG`:

cases.says: For a class with two public fields and no parent fields, all three lists are [x, y].
ownFields(Child) is [childPrivate, childPublic]: every access level, nothing inherited.
publicFields(GrandChild) holds the public fields of Child and Parent, though GrandChild declares none.
publicFields(Child) holds the TAG constant of the interface Child implements.
allFields(GrandChild) holds GrandChild's, Child's and Parent's fields, private ones too, in that order.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: getDeclaredFields() lists a class's own fields of every access level, while getFields() lists public fields including inherited ones.
